lessons.title: Scope, Focus, and Implication
lessons.learn: Distinguish assertion, presupposition, and invited inference through focus and lexical precision.

grammar.title: Focus and semantic scope
grammar.explain: Focus markers restrict alternatives; their position changes what is excluded. A C2 speaker can state which proposition was asserted and which conclusion remains inferential.

examples.en: The problem is not merely budgetary but also institutional.

examples.t: Fue precisamente la falta de consulta lo que generó rechazo.
examples.r: fue presisamente la falta de konsulta lo ke henero re haso
examples.en: It was precisely the lack of consultation that generated opposition.

examples.t: Que haya vuelto a protestar presupone que ya lo hizo antes.
examples.r: ke aya vuelto a protestar presupone ke ya lo iso antes
examples.en: That she protested again presupposes that she did so before.

lessons.title: Counterfactual Viewpoint and Evidential Distance
lessons.learn: Manipulate tense and mood to locate responsibility, regret, probability, and unreal alternatives.

grammar.title: Compound conditionals and viewpoint
grammar.explain: The pluperfect subjunctive plus conditional perfect constructs an unreal past. Evidential futures and conditionals can mark probability or reported distance rather than time alone.

lessons.title: Lo que el texto presupone: presuposición e implicatura
lessons.learn: A sentence smuggles in assumptions: ¿POR QUÉ IGNORÓ LA NORMA? presupposes the norm and the ignoring. C2 names the presupposition instead of arguing inside it: ESA PREGUNTA PARTE DE QUE …

grammar.title: Naming the presupposition
grammar.pattern: esa pregunta parte de que … · el texto da por hecho que … · eso no está probado
grammar.explain: Esa pregunta parte de que yo lo sabía. El párrafo da por hecho que hubo un incumplimiento — y eso no está probado. Naming the frame is how a Spanish speaker refuses the question without refusing to answer.

examples.t: Esa pregunta parte de que todos lo sabían.
examples.r: EH-sah preh-GOON-tah PAR-teh deh keh TOH-dohs loh sah-BEE-ahn.
examples.en: That question presupposes that everyone knew.

examples.t: El texto da por hecho que hubo un incumplimiento.
examples.r: el TEKS-toh dah por EH-choh keh OO-boh oon een-koom-plee-MYEN-toh.
examples.en: The text takes a breach for granted.

examples.t: Esa presuposición la rechazo.
examples.r: EH-sah preh-soo-poh-see-SYOHN lah reh-CHAH-soh.
examples.en: I reject that presupposition.

mistakes.wrong: ¿Por qué ignoró la norma? (as a first question)
mistakes.right: Antes de responder: ¿de dónde parte la pregunta?
mistakes.why: The question smuggles in the answer; break the frame first.

mistakes.wrong: El texto implica que fue así y lo prueba.
mistakes.right: El texto lo da por hecho; probarlo es otra cosa.

dialogue.t: ¿Por qué ignoró la norma?

dialogue.t: Esa pregunta parte de que la ignoré.
dialogue.r: EH-sah preh-GOON-tah PAR-teh deh keh lah ee-gnoh-REH.
dialogue.en: That question presupposes that I ignored it.

dialogue.t: ¿Y no fue así?
dialogue.r: ee noh fweh ah-SEE?
dialogue.en: And was it not so?

dialogue.t: El asunto está sin resolver. Antes de responder, aclaremos eso.
dialogue.r: el ah-SOON-toh es-TAH seen reh-sol-VEHR. AHN-tehs deh res-pohn-DEHR, ah-klah-REH-mohs EH-soh.
dialogue.en: The matter is unresolved. Before I answer, let's settle that.

lessons.title: Rhetoric, Irony, and Ethical Persuasion
lessons.learn: Analyse rhetorical framing and produce persuasive discourse without caricaturing opposing positions.

grammar.title: Rhetorical stance
grammar.explain: Irony depends on contextual mismatch, while concession can strengthen credibility. Ethical persuasion distinguishes evidence, warrant, and value judgment.
grammar.pattern: fair objection → concession → rebuttal → proportionate proposal

lessons.learn: Edit institutional prose for modality, agency, enforceability, and reader access.

grammar.title: Deontic modality and agency

lessons.title: Cambio de registro deliberado: administrativo, publicitario, lema
lessons.learn: A C2 text can fold in a register on purpose — a legal sentence quoted to be mocked, a slogan dropped into an essay. The frame signals it: «Suena a lenguaje administrativo cuando dice: …»

grammar.title: Quoting a register, and marking it
grammar.pattern: suena a … cuando dice: … · cito: … · con un lema: …
grammar.explain: Suena a lenguaje administrativo: «se procederá a la revisión». Con un lema: «primero revisar, después prometer». The frame bounds the borrowed register and keeps the irony legible.

lessons.title: El pronóstico calibrado: la incertidumbre con números
lessons.learn: Expert Spanish states its uncertainty on a scale: CONFIRMADO, PROBABLE, POSIBLE, NO DESCARTABLE, POCO PROBABLE — and names the horizon: A CORTO PLAZO, HASTA 2030. The forecast is only as good as the words around it.

grammar.title: Uncertainty scale
grammar.pattern: confirmado > probable > posible > no descartable > poco probable
grammar.explain: A corto plazo, una subida es probable; a largo plazo es posible, y una bajada no es descartable. Stating the horizon and the band makes a forecast falsifiable instead of rhetorical.

examples.t: A corto plazo, una subida es probable.
examples.r: ah KOR-toh PLAH-soh, OO-nah soo-BEE-dah es proh-BAH-bleh.
examples.en: In the short term a rise is probable.

examples.t: Una bajada no es descartable.
examples.r: OO-nah bah-HAH-dah noh es des-kar-TAH-bleh.
examples.en: A decline cannot be ruled out.

examples.t: El pronóstico vale hasta 2030.
examples.r: el proh-NOS-tee-koh BAH-leh AHS-tah dohs MEE-l treh-een-tah.
examples.en: The forecast holds until 2030.

mistakes.right: A corto plazo es probable que suba.
mistakes.why: A bare future assertion hides the horizon and the band.
Two hedges cancel; the scale takes one position.

culture.text: Spanish has a literature of quotation and reversal: Cervantes parodied the books of chivalry, Lorca borrowed the romance and changed its voice, and the press quotes a phrase in order to turn it. The practical effect at C2 is that allusion is normal: readers are expected to hear the borrowed line, which is why this level drills irony, parallelism and the deliberate clash of registers rather than more word lists.

reading.text: Un artículo empieza: «En un lugar de la Mancha no pasa nada — y eso es la noticia.» El autor cita a Cervantes para contradecirlo. Quien no oye la alusión lee solo una afirmación; quien la oye lee un movimiento: primero la fórmula prestada, luego su vuelta, luego la razón. Ese movimiento es el argumento, y sin él la cita solo adorna.
reading.gloss: An article begins: 'In a place in La Mancha nothing happens — and that is the news.' The author quotes Cervantes in order to contradict him. Whoever does not hear the allusion reads only a claim; whoever hears it reads a movement: first the borrowed formula, then its turn, then the reason. That movement is the argument, and without it the quotation merely decorates.

listening.script:
Entrevistadora: Su texto cita el Quijote y lo contradice.
Autor: Sí, y no es un riesgo si el lector lo conoce.
Entrevistadora: ¿Y si no lo conoce?
Autor: Entonces le queda la idea, que también funciona sola.
listening.gloss: Interviewer: Your text quotes Don Quixote and contradicts it. Author: Yes, and it is not a risk if the reader knows it. Interviewer: And if they don't? Author: Then the idea remains, which also works on its own.

mistakes.wrong: En un lugar de la Mancha, de cuyo nombre no quiero acordarme, no pasa nada.
mistakes.right: «En un lugar de la Mancha no pasa nada», parafraseando a Cervantes.
mistakes.why: An unmarked quotation reads as the author's own prose; a marked one is an allusion.

mistakes.wrong: Es un riesgo si el lector conoce o no lo conoce.
mistakes.right: No es un riesgo si el lector lo conoce.
mistakes.why: One condition per clause; the doubled alternative muddies the claim.

mistakes.wrong: La cita adorna y también prueba.
mistakes.right: La cita adorna; la prueba es otra cosa.
mistakes.why: A quotation illustrates; it never proves.

task.title: Quote, reverse, justify
task.instructions: Write one Spanish paragraph of C2 argument in three moves: quote a proverb or a literary line, reverse it, and justify the reversal with a case the original misses. Then cut every adjective that only adds emphasis and check whether the reversal still stands. If it does, the paragraph was an argument; if not, it was decoration.
